ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human safety reviewer with the full two-message chat transcript; no fare or fee adjustment and no account action is taken in this automated ruling. Reviewer to assess the 18:22 message [F4] against the driver's smoking request [F3] under SAFE-1, and to check whether the driver [F6] also filed a contemporaneous RydeHELP report. No flag_account is applied to either party at this stage.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety incident: the rider's message at 18:22, "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4], is an express threat of physical violence toward the driver, sent one minute after the driver's lawful request not to smoke in the car [F3], and it is preserved in a complete, fully timestamped two-message chat record [F5]. The driver separately reports the same threat in writing after the trip [F6]. Per SAFE-1 no automated ruling is made; the file goes to a human reviewer with this summary. For the reviewer's benefit the non-safety facts are clean and need no adjustment: the metered RydeTAXI fare of $21.26 corresponds to a route whose actual distance 8.8 km is 0.1 km shorter than the optimal 8.9 km [F1], over 13.3 min against a 16 min estimate [F2], so no unexempted off-route segment exists and the RD-1/RD-2 recoverable amount is zero; nothing in the driving record supports a dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-2 is not raised against the driver [F1][F2]. The parties' profiles — rider 3.6-year account, rating 4.5, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days [F7]; driver 2.0 years, rating 4.85, 427 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld [F8] — are context only and decide nothing [SAFE-1]. The only open question for the reviewer is what consequence, if any, attaches to the threat [F4].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate's own reading concedes the opposite of exculpation: the message at 18:22 [F4] is an express threat and corroborates rather than contradicts the driver's post-trip statement [F6]; being a system-recorded chat message it outweighs the statement, and on SAFE-1 the exchange is confirmed intimidation. Accepted only in so far as it supports escalation.

Accepted as to context — the 18:21 request [F3] was lawful and preceded the 18:22 message [F4] — but it does not avoid SAFE-1: escalation is mandatory precisely because the rider answered a lawful request with a threat of violence [F4][SAFE-1].
Accepted: escalation with a fact summary is the correct disposition [F4][F5][SAFE-1]; the record is complete and fully timestamped [F5].

Accepted as a factual observation only; no fare ruling is made in a safety case. The trace is neutral-to-clean: actual 8.8 km vs optimal 8.9 km [F1] and 13.3 min vs 16 min [F2], so RD-1/RD-2 yield zero in any event [RD-1][RD-2]. Recorded for the reviewer, not as an outcome.

Rejected as mitigation: profile facts cannot decide or attenuate a safety finding — the rider's 3.6-year account, rating 4.5 and 0 disputes in 90 days [F7], and the driver's clean record [F8], are context only and are not a basis for ruling [SAFE-1]; a clean history does not neutralise the express threat [F4].

Accepted as a fact but rejected as a basis for any finding: the GPS track [F1][F2] shows no deviation, so nothing arises against the driver under SAFE-2; but the absence of a driving allegation does not answer the rider's threat, which is assessed under SAFE-1 [F4].

Rejected as a basis for any action: the driver's profile — 2.0 years, 4.85 rating, 427 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld [F8] — is context only and cannot decide or dispose of the safety question [SAFE-1]; no account action against either party is taken in this ruling.
